```{r}
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(fpp3)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)

# -----------------------------
# 1. Data preparation
# -----------------------------

read_fred_cd <- function(series_id, term_months) {
  url <- paste0("https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=", series_id)

  read.csv(url) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      date = yearmonth(observation_date),
      term = term_months,
      rate = .data[[series_id]]
    ) |>
    select(date, term, rate) |>
    filter(
      date >= yearmonth("2021 Apr"),
      date <= yearmonth("2026 Apr"),
      !is.na(rate)
    )
}

cd <- bind_rows(
  read_fred_cd("NDR6MCD", 6),
  read_fred_cd("NDR12MCD", 12),
  read_fred_cd("NDR24MCD", 24)
) |>
  mutate(
    term = factor(
      term,
      levels = c(6, 12, 24),
      labels = c("6 Month", "12 Month", "24 Month")
    )
  ) |>
  as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)

min_date <- min(cd$date)
max_date <- max(cd$date)
max_future_date <- max_date + 24
term_choices <- levels(cd$term)
model_choices <- c("Mean", "ARIMA", "TSLM", "Naive", "Ensemble")

# -----------------------------
# 2. Helper functions
# -----------------------------

months_between <- function(start_ym, end_ym) {
  start_date <- as.Date(start_ym)
  end_date <- as.Date(end_ym)

  12 * (year(end_date) - year(start_date)) +
    (month(end_date) - month(start_date))
}

seasonally_adjust_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = season_adjust) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

detrend_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = rate - trend) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

fit_forecast_models <- function(data, selected_term, holdout_size, horizon) {
  one_series <- data |>
    filter(term == selected_term) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    select(date, rate) |>
    arrange(date) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date)

  req(holdout_size < nrow(one_series))

  train_n <- nrow(one_series) - holdout_size

  train <- one_series |>
    slice_head(n = train_n)

  test <- one_series |>
    slice_tail(n = holdout_size)

  fits <- train |>
    model(
      Mean = MEAN(rate),
      Naive = NAIVE(rate),
      ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
      TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
    )

  test_fc_base <- fits |>
    forecast(h = holdout_size) |>
    as_tibble()

  future_fc_base <- fits |>
    forecast(h = horizon) |>
    as_tibble()

  test_fc_ensemble <- test_fc_base |>
    group_by(date) |>
    summarise(
      .model = "Ensemble",
      .mean = mean(.mean, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  future_fc_ensemble <- future_fc_base |>
    group_by(date) |>
    summarise(
      .model = "Ensemble",
      .mean = mean(.mean, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  test_fc <- bind_rows(
    test_fc_base |> select(.model, date, .mean),
    test_fc_ensemble
  )

  future_fc <- bind_rows(
    future_fc_base |> select(.model, date, .mean),
    future_fc_ensemble
  )

  acc <- test_fc |>
    left_join(test |> as_tibble(), by = "date") |>
    group_by(.model) |>
    summarise(
      ME = mean(rate - .mean, na.rm = TRUE),
      RMSE = sqrt(mean((rate - .mean)^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
      MAE = mean(abs(rate - .mean), na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(RMSE)

  list(
    train = train,
    test = test,
    fits = fits,
    test_fc = test_fc,
    future_fc = future_fc,
    accuracy = acc
  )
}

get_simulation_rates <- function(data, invest_ym, selected_model) {
  if (invest_ym <= max_date) {
    data |>
      filter(date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      mutate(rate_source = "Observed historical rate")
  } else {
    h_needed <- months_between(max_date, invest_ym)

    fits <- data |>
      model(
        Mean = MEAN(rate),
        Naive = NAIVE(rate),
        ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
        TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
      )

    fc_base <- fits |>
      forecast(h = h_needed) |>
      as_tibble()

    fc_ensemble <- fc_base |>
      group_by(term, date) |>
      summarise(
        .model = "Ensemble",
        .mean = mean(.mean, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      )

    fc_all <- bind_rows(
      fc_base |> select(.model, date, term, .mean),
      fc_ensemble
    )

    fc_all |>
      filter(.model == selected_model, date == invest_ym) |>
      transmute(
        date,
        term,
        rate = .mean,
        rate_source = paste(selected_model, "forecast")
      )
  }
}

plot_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "#6b7280"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#e5e7eb"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )

# -----------------------------
# 4. Server
# -----------------------------

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  explore_base <- reactive({
    req(input$explore_terms)

    cd |>
      filter(
        term %in% input$explore_terms,
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      )
  })

  output$latest_date_summary <- renderText({
    max(explore_base()$date) |> as.character()
  })

  output$highest_latest_rate_summary <- renderText({
    data <- explore_base()

    latest <- data |>
      as_tibble() |>
      filter(date == max(date)) |>
      arrange(desc(rate)) |>
      slice(1)

    paste0(round(latest$rate, 2), "%")
  })

  output$direction_summary <- renderText({
    data <- explore_base()

    latest_two <- data |>
      as_tibble() |>
      filter(term == "12 Month") |>
      arrange(date) |>
      slice_tail(n = 2)

    if (nrow(latest_two) < 2) {
      return("N/A")
    }

    if (latest_two$rate[2] > latest_two$rate[1]) {
      "Rising"
    } else if (latest_two$rate[2] < latest_two$rate[1]) {
      "Falling"
    } else {
      "Flat"
    }
  })

  output$core_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_sa) seasonally_adjust_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      autoplot(rate, linewidth = 1.05) +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_sa,
          "Seasonally Adjusted National Average CD Rates",
          "National Average CD Rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Term"
      ) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("#ff8200", "#4b5563", "#9ca3af")) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$seasonal_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_detrended) detrend_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      gg_season(rate, labels = "both") +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_detrended,
          "Detrended Seasonal Plot",
          "Seasonal Plot"
        ),
        x = "Month",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Year"
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$spread_plot <- renderPlot({
    spread_data <- cd |>
      as_tibble() |>
      filter(
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      ) |>
      select(date, term, rate) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = rate) |>
      mutate(
        `24 minus 6 Month` = `24 Month` - `6 Month`,
        `12 minus 6 Month` = `12 Month` - `6 Month`
      ) |>
      select(date, `24 minus 6 Month`, `12 minus 6 Month`) |>
      pivot_longer(
        -date,
        names_to = "spread",
        values_to = "value"
      ) |>
      filter(!is.na(value))

    ggplot(spread_data, aes(x = date, y = value, color = spread)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#6b7280") +
      labs(
        title = "CD Term Spreads",
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate spread, percentage points",
        color = "Spread"
      ) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("#ff8200", "#4b5563")) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$decomp_plot <- renderPlot({
    one_series <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$decomp_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date) |>
      as_tsibble(index = date)

    if (input$decomp_type == "STL") {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
        components()
    } else {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(classical_decomposition(rate, type = "additive")) |>
        components()
    }

    autoplot(fit) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          input$decomp_type,
          "decomposition for",
          input$decomp_term,
          "CD rates"
        )
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  forecast_results <- reactive({
    fit_forecast_models(
      cd,
      input$forecast_term,
      input$holdout,
      input$horizon
    )
  })

  output$selected_model_summary <- renderText({
    input$forecast_model
  })

  output$best_model_summary <- renderText({
    forecast_results()$accuracy$.model[1]
  })

  output$horizon_summary <- renderText({
    paste0(input$horizon, " mo.")
  })

  output$forecast_plot <- renderPlot({
    res <- forecast_results()

    model_to_show <- input$forecast_model

    fc <- res$future_fc |>
      filter(.model == model_to_show)

    history <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$forecast_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date)

    ggplot() +
      geom_line(
        data = history,
        aes(x = date, y = rate),
        linewidth = 1.05,
        color = "#4b5563"
      ) +
      geom_line(
        data = fc,
        aes(x = date, y = .mean),
        linewidth = 1.15,
        color = "#ff8200"
      ) +
      geom_point(
        data = fc,
        aes(x = date, y = .mean),
        size = 2,
        color = "#ff8200"
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          model_to_show,
          "forecast for",
          input$forecast_term,
          "CD rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)"
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$accuracy_table <- renderTable({
    forecast_results()$accuracy |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(.model, ME, RMSE, MAE) |>
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
  })

  output$forecast_recommendation <- renderText({
    acc <- forecast_results()$accuracy
    best <- acc$.model[1]

    paste0(
      "Recommended model based on current holdout: ", best, "\n\n",
      "Reason: it has the lowest RMSE on the selected holdout period. RMSE is useful here because CD rates are measured in percentage points and larger errors are penalized more heavily. The Ensemble model averages the Mean, Naive, ARIMA, and TSLM forecasts, which can make the forecast more stable by reducing dependence on a single model assumption. However, because CD rates are highly persistent, ARIMA and Naive may still outperform the Ensemble in some holdout windows.","\n\n","Tip: The Ensemble Model is a combination of Mean, Naive, ARIMA, and TSLM models by averaging their predicted values. Rather than relying on just one method, this model increases stability and limits the forecast's dependence on a singular model's accuracy."
    )
  })

  sim_data <- reactive({
    invest_ym <- yearmonth(input$invest_date)

    sim_rates <- get_simulation_rates(
      data = cd,
      invest_ym = invest_ym,
      selected_model = input$sim_model
    )

    validate(
      need(nrow(sim_rates) > 0, "No rates are available for the selected investment month.")
    )

    sim_rates |>
      mutate(
        term_months = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(term), "\\d+")),
        initial_amount = input$initial_amount,
        maturity_value = initial_amount * (1 + rate / 100 / 12) ^ term_months,
        interest_earned = maturity_value - initial_amount
      )
  })

  output$sim_plot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(sim_data(), aes(x = term, y = maturity_value, fill = term)) +
      geom_col(show.legend = FALSE, width = 0.65) +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2))),
        vjust = -0.4,
        fontface = "bold"
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          "Projected Value at CD Maturity",
          ifelse(
            yearmonth(input$invest_date) > max_date,
            paste("using", input$sim_model, "forecasted rates"),
            "using observed historical rates"
          )
        ),
        x = "CD Term",
        y = "Maturity value"
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("#ff8200", "#4b5563", "#9ca3af")) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$sim_table <- renderTable({
    sim_data() |>
      transmute(
        Term = term,
        `Investment Month` = as.character(date),
        `Rate Source` = rate_source,
        `Rate (%)` = round(rate, 3),
        `Initial Amount` = dollar(initial_amount),
        `Estimated Maturity Value` = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2)),
        `Estimated Interest Earned` = dollar(round(interest_earned, 2))
      )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

```

# Construction

## 0. Instructions

### Goal
Build an interactive tool around a time series dataset of your choosing and create an app that:
1. Supports exploratory and historical analysis of the series.
2. Compares forecasting approaches using tools from class.
3. Includes one extension beyond standard forecasting:
    - Option 1 (Model Extension) - Implement and explain a forecasting method not covered in class.
    - Option 2 (Causal Extension) - Implement difference-in-differences or synthetic control and interpret the results.

### Deliverables:
1. Interactive app (shiny is recommended)
2. Supporting code (models, diagnostics, data preparation steps, etc.)
3. User Guide (how to use app and interpret outputs)
4. Exit Interview (short conversation to assess conceptual understanding and ownershup of the project)

### Dataset Requirements:
1. Temporal Structure: Must be a true time series indexed by time. If irregular, series must be regularized or aggregated to work with tools.
- daily, weekly, monthly (at least 3 years)
- quarterly (at least 8 years)
2. Interesting: Must have at least one of the following:
- Interpretable trend, seasonality, or structural change.
- External events that can be annotated.
- A clear real world generating process that can be explained.
3. Scope and Feasibility: Data should require light-to-moderate cleaning. Multiple series are allowed, but must center on one primary time index.
4. Overused Dataset Guidance: Common classroom examples (e.g. air passengers, stock indices, weather normals, etc.) are ones to be avoided. Stock prices are tempting but historically they make for harder analysis through our lens (our tools don't work well with stock prices).

### Tool Requirements
1. Historical and Exploratory Analysis
-  Core time series plot.
- Seasonal visualization.
- One additional visualization that's interesting for your series.
- Clear annotation and interpretations.
2. Forecasting
- One baseline model (e.g. mean, naive, seasonal naive, etc.)
- Two statistical forecasting models from class (e.g. TSLM, ETS, ARIMA, NNETAR)
- Forecast comparison using appropriate accuracy metrics.
- A clear recommendation on which model to use and why.
3. Extension
- Option 1 (Model Extension): 
    - Implement a forecasting method not covered in class.
    - Explain at a high level how it works and when it might be preferred.
- Option 2 (Causal Extension):
    - Implement DiD or Synthetic Control
    - Emphasize interpretation, diagnostics, and limitations.
4. Interactivity
- An input to adjust the date range shown in all visuals.
- An input to toggle your "core time series plot" between original data and a seasonally adjusted version.
- An input to toggle your "seasonal visualization" between the original data and a detrended version.
- An imput to adjust forecast horizon (with sensible deafulkt value in series context)

### Possible App Structure
Tabs: Introduction/User Guide, Explore, Decompse, Forecast, Diagnostics, Causal (if applicable).

## A. Shiny App Structure

### User Guide

**Purpose**

Welcome to the CD Rate Forecasting Explorer. This tool is designed to explore and explain historical rates for six, twelve, and twenty four month Certificates of Deposit (CDs) and to provide forecasts for future rates. To provide the best representation of practical rates facing consumers, this tool is based on National Average Rate of CDs (respective to their term length), coming from the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) database, which records the typical (average) rates offered by banks and instituitions to consumers from April 2021 to April 2026. 

**Directions**

***Explore Tab:*** Visualize the series over time by selecting which series to view, and the range of time displayed. Use the Time Series Plot to view the overall series and the Seasonal Plot to compare seasonal patterns. To gain a better understanding of the visualizations, select the "Seasonally Adjusted" and "Detrended" options for the Core Time Series and Seasonal Plots, respectively, which give a clearer picture of the underlying patterns in the trend and seasonality.

***Decompose Tab:*** Dive deeper into each component of a series by selecting one of the three and selecting either a Classical or STL decomposition model. Use the output to understand the relative importance of trend, seasonality, and remainder in the series and to identify any structural changes or anomalies. This can give a good view into the true changes/patterns in rates.

***Forecast Tab:*** Make predictions of future rates! Select which CD term to forecast from the drop down menu, then adjust the forecast horizon to determine how far in advance you'd like the forecast to be. To explore different forecasting possibilities, choose from ARIMA or TSLM models, and alter the holdout set. 
Tip: The optimal model is displayed by default. This model is determined by selecting the forecast method and holdout size that minimizes error metrics as much as possible. Due to uncertainty, other models could, in theory, prove more accurate despite having larger error metrics, giving the option to adjust them some reasoning. "All models are wrong, some are useful" - Adam Petrie.

***Simulator:*** Put the forecasts to use. Select an investment date and initial amount, then use the visualizations to simulate the different returns based on that initial investment.

### Annotations and Interpretation

##### Explore
Core Time Series Plot: Each series follows a similar trend and general movement, starting at or near zero in 2021, reflecting the low rates associated with the post-COVID economy. In early 2022, each rises sharply, possibly aligning with the aggressive Fed tightening and rapid repricing of short term investment options at the time. Counterintuitively, rates of longer term options do not increase more rapidly than those of shorter terms. In other words, longer term CDs typically do not offer higher rates (especially at their respective peaks). However this difference in rate begins to converge in more recent observations following the conversion to a downward trend, leading to the  assumption that the current market is expecting rates to decline in the future.

Seasonal Plot: Rates do not exhibit any true seasonality as the plot reveals no similar movements or values within similar times in the year. This inconsistent pattern suggests that changes that appear to correspond in time may be caused by the similar timing of external political or economic factors, not rates themselves. Important insight, yes, but regardless not true seasonality.

Term Spread: An upward sloping line indicates a higher yield for longer term CD rates, a downward sloping curve indicates a higher yield for shorter terms. This spread validates the observation of rate comparison from the core plot, revealing a domination of shorter term rates,

Higher points in the line indicate a greater difference in rates paid on the respective shorter and longer term CDs (6 month vs. 12 month, 6 month vs. 24 month). As the plot treads closer to zero (dashed line), the benefit of a longer term decreases. The upward trend on the left side and its change to a downward trend verifies the observations in the core plot, revealing the diminishing benefit of longer term CDs since the peak, along with the convergence of rates in more recent observations.

##### Decompose
STL decomposition model performs slightly better than classical. Sharp increasing trend converts into a mild to moderate downward trend.Seasonality is practically non-existent, indicated by the miniscule range in the y-axis (large vertical bar).

##### Forecast
The optimal forecasting model alternates between Naive and ARIMA depending on holdout test size. A size of 8, 9, 10, and 16 favors the Naive model, whereas everything else in the 6-18 month range favors ARIMA. Although the ARIMA appears best more frequently, the model that exhibits the lowest possible RMSE is Naive with a holdout size of 10 months, proving it as the best recommendation.

##### Simulator

Due to the illiquidity of CDs, the rate at which a CD is opened cannot change. Calculating its value at endowment is done by simply using the rate observed at the date it is opened. If the investment date selected is outside the scope of the data, the corresponding rate is determined from the forecasting model selected.


## B. Shiny App Building

v1
```{r}
library(shiny)
library(fpp3)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)

# -----------------------------
# 1. Data preparation
# -----------------------------

read_fred_cd <- function(series_id, term_months) {
  url <- paste0("https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=", series_id)

  read.csv(url) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      date = yearmonth(observation_date),
      term = term_months,
      rate = .data[[series_id]]
    ) |>
    select(date, term, rate) |>
    filter(
      date >= yearmonth("2021 Apr"),
      date <= yearmonth("2026 Apr"),
      !is.na(rate)
    )
}

cd <- bind_rows(
  read_fred_cd("NDR6MCD", 6),
  read_fred_cd("NDR12MCD", 12),
  read_fred_cd("NDR24MCD", 24)
) |>
  mutate(
    term = factor(
      term,
      levels = c(6, 12, 24),
      labels = c("6 Month", "12 Month", "24 Month")
    )
  ) |>
  as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)

min_date <- min(cd$date)
max_date <- max(cd$date)
term_choices <- levels(cd$term)

# -----------------------------
# 2. Helper functions
# -----------------------------

seasonally_adjust_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = season_adjust) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

detrend_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = rate - trend) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

fit_forecast_models <- function(data, selected_term, holdout_size, horizon) {
  one_series <- data |>
    filter(term == selected_term) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    select(date, rate) |>
    arrange(date) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date)

  req(holdout_size < nrow(one_series))

  train_n <- nrow(one_series) - holdout_size

  train <- one_series |>
    slice_head(n = train_n)

  test <- one_series |>
    slice_tail(n = holdout_size)

  fits <- train |>
    model(
      Naive = NAIVE(rate),
      ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
      TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
    )

  test_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = holdout_size)

  future_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = horizon)

  acc <- test_fc |>
    accuracy(test) |>
    arrange(RMSE)

  list(
    train = train,
    test = test,
    fits = fits,
    test_fc = test_fc,
    future_fc = future_fc,
    accuracy = acc
  )
}

# -----------------------------
# 3. UI
# -----------------------------

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  explore_base <- reactive({
    req(input$explore_terms)

    cd |>
      filter(
        term %in% input$explore_terms,
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      )
  })

  output$core_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_sa) seasonally_adjust_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      autoplot(rate) +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_sa,
          "Seasonally Adjusted National Average CD Rates",
          "National Average CD Rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Term"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$seasonal_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_detrended) detrend_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      gg_season(rate, labels = "both") +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_detrended,
          "Detrended Seasonal Plot",
          "Seasonal Plot"
        ),
        x = "Month",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Year"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$spread_plot <- renderPlot({
    spread_data <- cd |>
      as_tibble() |>
      filter(
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      ) |>
      select(date, term, rate) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = rate) |>
      mutate(
        `24 minus 6 Month` = `24 Month` - `6 Month`,
        `12 minus 6 Month` = `12 Month` - `6 Month`
      ) |>
      select(date, `24 minus 6 Month`, `12 minus 6 Month`) |>
      pivot_longer(
        -date,
        names_to = "spread",
        values_to = "value"
      )

    ggplot(spread_data, aes(x = date, y = value, color = spread)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
      labs(
        title = "CD Term Spreads",
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate spread, percentage points",
        color = "Spread"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$decomp_plot <- renderPlot({
    one_series <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$decomp_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date) |>
      as_tsibble(index = date)

    if (input$decomp_type == "STL") {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
        components()
    } else {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(classical_decomposition(rate, type = "additive")) |>
        components()
    }

    autoplot(fit) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          input$decomp_type,
          "decomposition for",
          input$decomp_term,
          "CD rates"
        )
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  forecast_results <- reactive({
    fit_forecast_models(
      cd,
      input$forecast_term,
      input$holdout,
      input$horizon
    )
  })

  output$forecast_plot <- renderPlot({
    res <- forecast_results()
    acc <- res$accuracy

    model_to_show <- input$forecast_model

    if (model_to_show == "Best by RMSE") {
      model_to_show <- acc$.model[1]
    }

    fc <- res$future_fc |>
      filter(.model == model_to_show)

    history <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$forecast_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date) |>
      as_tsibble(index = date)

    autoplot(fc, history) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          model_to_show,
          "forecast for",
          input$forecast_term,
          "CD rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$accuracy_table <- renderTable({
    forecast_results()$accuracy |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(.model, ME, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, MASE) |>
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
  })

  output$forecast_recommendation <- renderText({
    acc <- forecast_results()$accuracy
    best <- acc$.model[1]

    paste0(
      "Recommended model: ", best, "\n\n",
      "Reason: it has the lowest RMSE on the selected holdout period. RMSE is useful here because CD rates are measured in percentage points and larger errors are penalized more heavily. Still, the recommendation can change if the holdout size changes, so the app allows sensitivity checks."
    )
  })

  sim_data <- reactive({
    invest_ym <- yearmonth(input$invest_date)

    cd |>
      filter(date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      mutate(
        term_months = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(term), "\\d+")),
        initial_amount = input$initial_amount,
        maturity_value = initial_amount * (1 + rate / 100 / 12) ^ term_months,
        interest_earned = maturity_value - initial_amount
      )
  })

  output$sim_plot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(sim_data(), aes(x = term, y = maturity_value, fill = term)) +
      geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2))),
        vjust = -0.4
      ) +
      labs(
        title = "Projected Value at CD Maturity",
        x = "CD Term",
        y = "Maturity value"
      ) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$sim_table <- renderTable({
    sim_data() |>
      transmute(
        Term = term,
        `Investment Month` = as.character(date),
        `Rate (%)` = round(rate, 3),
        `Initial Amount` = dollar(initial_amount),
        `Estimated Maturity Value` = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2)),
        `Estimated Interest Earned` = dollar(round(interest_earned, 2))
      )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(fpp3)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)

# -----------------------------
# 1. Data preparation
# -----------------------------

read_fred_cd <- function(series_id, term_months) {
  url <- paste0("https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=", series_id)

  read.csv(url) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      date = yearmonth(observation_date),
      term = term_months,
      rate = .data[[series_id]]
    ) |>
    select(date, term, rate) |>
    filter(
      date >= yearmonth("2021 Apr"),
      date <= yearmonth("2026 Apr"),
      !is.na(rate)
    )
}

cd <- bind_rows(
  read_fred_cd("NDR6MCD", 6),
  read_fred_cd("NDR12MCD", 12),
  read_fred_cd("NDR24MCD", 24)
) |>
  mutate(
    term = factor(
      term,
      levels = c(6, 12, 24),
      labels = c("6 Month", "12 Month", "24 Month")
    )
  ) |>
  as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)

min_date <- min(cd$date)
max_date <- max(cd$date)
max_future_date <- max_date + 24
term_choices <- levels(cd$term)
model_choices <- c("Mean", "ARIMA", "TSLM", "Naive")

# -----------------------------
# 2. Helper functions
# -----------------------------

months_between <- function(start_ym, end_ym) {
  start_date <- as.Date(start_ym)
  end_date <- as.Date(end_ym)

  12 * (year(end_date) - year(start_date)) +
    (month(end_date) - month(start_date))
}

seasonally_adjust_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = season_adjust) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

detrend_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = rate - trend) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

fit_forecast_models <- function(data, selected_term, holdout_size, horizon) {
  one_series <- data |>
    filter(term == selected_term) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    select(date, rate) |>
    arrange(date) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date)

  req(holdout_size < nrow(one_series))

  train_n <- nrow(one_series) - holdout_size

  train <- one_series |>
    slice_head(n = train_n)

  test <- one_series |>
    slice_tail(n = holdout_size)

  fits <- train |>
    model(
      Mean = MEAN(rate),
      Naive = NAIVE(rate),
      ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
      TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
    )

  test_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = holdout_size)

  future_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = horizon)

  acc <- test_fc |>
    accuracy(test) |>
    arrange(RMSE)

  list(
    train = train,
    test = test,
    fits = fits,
    test_fc = test_fc,
    future_fc = future_fc,
    accuracy = acc
  )
}

get_simulation_rates <- function(data, invest_ym, selected_model) {
  if (invest_ym <= max_date) {
    data |>
      filter(date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      mutate(rate_source = "Observed historical rate")
  } else {
    h_needed <- months_between(max_date, invest_ym)

    fits <- data |>
      model(
        Mean = MEAN(rate),
        Naive = NAIVE(rate),
        ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
        TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
      )

    fits |>
      forecast(h = h_needed) |>
      filter(.model == selected_model, date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      transmute(
        date,
        term,
        rate = .mean,
        rate_source = paste(selected_model, "forecast")
      )
  }
}

# -----------------------------
# 3. UI
# -----------------------------

# 4. Server

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  explore_base <- reactive({
    req(input$explore_terms)

    cd |>
      filter(
        term %in% input$explore_terms,
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      )
  })

  output$core_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_sa) seasonally_adjust_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      autoplot(rate) +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_sa,
          "Seasonally Adjusted National Average CD Rates",
          "National Average CD Rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Term"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$seasonal_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_detrended) detrend_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      gg_season(rate, labels = "both") +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_detrended,
          "Detrended Seasonal Plot",
          "Seasonal Plot"
        ),
        x = "Month",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Year"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$spread_plot <- renderPlot({
    spread_data <- cd |>
      as_tibble() |>
      filter(
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      ) |>
      select(date, term, rate) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = rate) |>
      mutate(
        `24 minus 6 Month` = `24 Month` - `6 Month`,
        `12 minus 6 Month` = `12 Month` - `6 Month`
      ) |>
      select(date, `24 minus 6 Month`, `12 minus 6 Month`) |>
      pivot_longer(
        -date,
        names_to = "spread",
        values_to = "value"
      ) |>
      filter(!is.na(value))

    ggplot(spread_data, aes(x = date, y = value, color = spread)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
      labs(
        title = "CD Term Spreads",
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate spread, percentage points",
        color = "Spread"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$decomp_plot <- renderPlot({
    one_series <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$decomp_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date) |>
      as_tsibble(index = date)

    if (input$decomp_type == "STL") {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
        components()
    } else {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(classical_decomposition(rate, type = "additive")) |>
        components()
    }

    autoplot(fit) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          input$decomp_type,
          "decomposition for",
          input$decomp_term,
          "CD rates"
        )
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  forecast_results <- reactive({
    fit_forecast_models(
      cd,
      input$forecast_term,
      input$holdout,
      input$horizon
    )
  })

  output$forecast_plot <- renderPlot({
    res <- forecast_results()

    model_to_show <- input$forecast_model

    fc <- res$future_fc |>
      filter(.model == model_to_show)

    history <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$forecast_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date) |>
      as_tsibble(index = date)

    autoplot(fc, history) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          model_to_show,
          "forecast for",
          input$forecast_term,
          "CD rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$accuracy_table <- renderTable({
    forecast_results()$accuracy |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(.model, ME, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, MASE) |>
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
  })

  output$forecast_recommendation <- renderText({
    acc <- forecast_results()$accuracy
    best <- acc$.model[1]

    paste0(
      "Recommended model: ", best, "\n\n",
      "Reason: it has the lowest RMSE on the selected holdout period. RMSE is useful here because CD rates are measured in percentage points and larger errors are penalized more heavily. Still, the recommendation can change if the holdout size changes, so the app allows sensitivity checks."
    )
  })

  sim_data <- reactive({
    invest_ym <- yearmonth(input$invest_date)

    sim_rates <- get_simulation_rates(
      data = cd,
      invest_ym = invest_ym,
      selected_model = input$sim_model
    )

    validate(
      need(nrow(sim_rates) > 0, "No rates are available for the selected investment month.")
    )

    sim_rates |>
      mutate(
        term_months = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(term), "\\d+")),
        initial_amount = input$initial_amount,
        maturity_value = initial_amount * (1 + rate / 100 / 12) ^ term_months,
        interest_earned = maturity_value - initial_amount
      )
  })

  output$sim_plot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(sim_data(), aes(x = term, y = maturity_value, fill = term)) +
      geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2))),
        vjust = -0.4
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          "Projected Value at CD Maturity",
          ifelse(
            yearmonth(input$invest_date) > max_date,
            paste("using", input$sim_model, "forecasted rates"),
            "using observed historical rates"
          )
        ),
        x = "CD Term",
        y = "Maturity value"
      ) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$sim_table <- renderTable({
    sim_data() |>
      transmute(
        Term = term,
        `Investment Month` = as.character(date),
        `Rate Source` = rate_source,
        `Rate (%)` = round(rate, 3),
        `Initial Amount` = dollar(initial_amount),
        `Estimated Maturity Value` = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2)),
        `Estimated Interest Earned` = dollar(round(interest_earned, 2))
      )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

```{r}
# 1. Data preparation

    as_tibble() |>
    select(date, rate) |>
    arrange(date) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date)

  req(holdout_size < nrow(one_series))

  train_n <- nrow(one_series) - holdout_size

  train <- one_series |>
    slice_head(n = train_n)

  test <- one_series |>
    slice_tail(n = holdout_size)

  fits <- train |>
    model(
      Mean = MEAN(rate),
      Naive = NAIVE(rate),
      ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
      TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
    )

  test_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = holdout_size)

  future_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = horizon)

  acc <- test_fc |>
    accuracy(test) |>
    arrange(RMSE)

  list(
    train = train,
    test = test,
    fits = fits,
    test_fc = test_fc,
    future_fc = future_fc,
    accuracy = acc
  )
}

get_simulation_rates <- function(data, invest_ym, selected_model) {
  if (invest_ym <= max_date) {
    data |>
      filter(date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      mutate(rate_source = "Observed historical rate")
  } else {
    h_needed <- months_between(max_date, invest_ym)

    fits <- data |>
      model(
        Mean = MEAN(rate),
        Naive = NAIVE(rate),
        ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
        TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
      )

    fits |>
      forecast(h = h_needed) |>
      filter(.model == selected_model, date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      transmute(
        date,
        term,
        rate = .mean,
        rate_source = paste(selected_model, "forecast")
      )
  }
}

# 4. Server
# -----------------------------

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  explore_base <- reactive({
    req(input$explore_terms)

    cd |>
      filter(
        term %in% input$explore_terms,
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      )
  })

  output$core_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_sa) seasonally_adjust_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      autoplot(rate) +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_sa,
          "Seasonally Adjusted National Average CD Rates",
          "National Average CD Rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Term"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$seasonal_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_detrended) detrend_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      gg_season(rate, labels = "both") +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_detrended,
          "Detrended Seasonal Plot",
          "Seasonal Plot"
        ),
        x = "Month",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Year"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$spread_plot <- renderPlot({
    spread_data <- cd |>
      as_tibble() |>
      filter(
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      ) |>
      select(date, term, rate) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = rate) |>
      mutate(
        `24 minus 6 Month` = `24 Month` - `6 Month`,
        `12 minus 6 Month` = `12 Month` - `6 Month`
      ) |>
      select(date, `24 minus 6 Month`, `12 minus 6 Month`) |>
      pivot_longer(
        -date,
        names_to = "spread",
        values_to = "value"
      ) |>
      filter(!is.na(value))

    ggplot(spread_data, aes(x = date, y = value, color = spread)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
      labs(
        title = "CD Term Spreads",
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate spread, percentage points",
        color = "Spread"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$decomp_plot <- renderPlot({
    one_series <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$decomp_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date) |>
      as_tsibble(index = date)

    if (input$decomp_type == "STL") {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
        components()
    } else {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(classical_decomposition(rate, type = "additive")) |>
        components()
    }

    autoplot(fit) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          input$decomp_type,
          "decomposition for",
          input$decomp_term,
          "CD rates"
        )
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  forecast_results <- reactive({
    fit_forecast_models(
      cd,
      input$forecast_term,
      input$holdout,
      input$horizon
    )
  })

  output$forecast_plot <- renderPlot({
    res <- forecast_results()

    model_to_show <- input$forecast_model

    fc <- res$future_fc |>
      filter(.model == model_to_show)

    history <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$forecast_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date) |>
      as_tsibble(index = date)

    autoplot(fc, history) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          model_to_show,
          "forecast for",
          input$forecast_term,
          "CD rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$accuracy_table <- renderTable({
    forecast_results()$accuracy |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(.model, ME, RMSE, MAE) |>
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
  })

  output$forecast_recommendation <- renderText({
    acc <- forecast_results()$accuracy
    best <- acc$.model[1]

    paste0(
      "Recommended model based on current holdout: ", best, "\n\n",
      "Reason: it has the lowest RMSE on the selected holdout period. RMSE is useful here because CD rates are measured in percentage points and larger errors are penalized more heavily. Still, the recommendation can change if the holdout size changes, so the app allows sensitivity checks. A holdout size of 8, 9, 10, and 16 months favors the Naive model, whereas everything else in the 6-18 month range favors ARIMA."
    )
  })

  sim_data <- reactive({
    invest_ym <- yearmonth(input$invest_date)

    sim_rates <- get_simulation_rates(
      data = cd,
      invest_ym = invest_ym,
      selected_model = input$sim_model
    )

    validate(
      need(nrow(sim_rates) > 0, "No rates are available for the selected investment month.")
    )

    sim_rates |>
      mutate(
        term_months = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(term), "\\d+")),
        initial_amount = input$initial_amount,
        maturity_value = initial_amount * (1 + rate / 100 / 12) ^ term_months,
        interest_earned = maturity_value - initial_amount
      )
  })

  output$sim_plot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(sim_data(), aes(x = term, y = maturity_value, fill = term)) +
      geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2))),
        vjust = -0.4
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          "Projected Value at CD Maturity",
          ifelse(
            yearmonth(input$invest_date) > max_date,
            paste("using", input$sim_model, "forecasted rates"),
            "using observed historical rates"
          )
        ),
        x = "CD Term",
        y = "Maturity value"
      ) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
      theme_minimal()
  })

  output$sim_table <- renderTable({
    sim_data() |>
      transmute(
        Term = term,
        `Investment Month` = as.character(date),
        `Rate Source` = rate_source,
        `Rate (%)` = round(rate, 3),
        `Initial Amount` = dollar(initial_amount),
        `Estimated Maturity Value` = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2)),
        `Estimated Interest Earned` = dollar(round(interest_earned, 2))
      )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(fpp3)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)

# -----------------------------
# 1. Data preparation
# -----------------------------

read_fred_cd <- function(series_id, term_months) {
  url <- paste0("https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=", series_id)

  read.csv(url) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      date = yearmonth(observation_date),
      term = term_months,
      rate = .data[[series_id]]
    ) |>
    select(date, term, rate) |>
    filter(
      date >= yearmonth("2021 Apr"),
      date <= yearmonth("2026 Apr"),
      !is.na(rate)
    )
}

cd <- bind_rows(
  read_fred_cd("NDR6MCD", 6),
  read_fred_cd("NDR12MCD", 12),
  read_fred_cd("NDR24MCD", 24)
) |>
  mutate(
    term = factor(
      term,
      levels = c(6, 12, 24),
      labels = c("6 Month", "12 Month", "24 Month")
    )
  ) |>
  as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)

min_date <- min(cd$date)
max_date <- max(cd$date)
max_future_date <- max_date + 24
term_choices <- levels(cd$term)
model_choices <- c("Mean", "ARIMA", "TSLM", "Naive")

# -----------------------------
# 2. Helper functions
# -----------------------------

months_between <- function(start_ym, end_ym) {
  start_date <- as.Date(start_ym)
  end_date <- as.Date(end_ym)

  12 * (year(end_date) - year(start_date)) +
    (month(end_date) - month(start_date))
}

seasonally_adjust_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = season_adjust) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

detrend_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = rate - trend) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

fit_forecast_models <- function(data, selected_term, holdout_size, horizon) {
  one_series <- data |>
    filter(term == selected_term) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    select(date, rate) |>
    arrange(date) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date)

  req(holdout_size < nrow(one_series))

  train_n <- nrow(one_series) - holdout_size

  train <- one_series |>
    slice_head(n = train_n)

  test <- one_series |>
    slice_tail(n = holdout_size)

  fits <- train |>
    model(
      Mean = MEAN(rate),
      Naive = NAIVE(rate),
      ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
      TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
    )

  test_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = holdout_size)

  future_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = horizon)

  acc <- test_fc |>
    accuracy(test) |>
    arrange(RMSE)

  list(
    train = train,
    test = test,
    fits = fits,
    test_fc = test_fc,
    future_fc = future_fc,
    accuracy = acc
  )
}

get_simulation_rates <- function(data, invest_ym, selected_model) {
  if (invest_ym <= max_date) {
    data |>
      filter(date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      mutate(rate_source = "Observed historical rate")
  } else {
    h_needed <- months_between(max_date, invest_ym)

    fits <- data |>
      model(
        Mean = MEAN(rate),
        Naive = NAIVE(rate),
        ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
        TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
      )

    fits |>
      forecast(h = h_needed) |>
      filter(.model == selected_model, date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      transmute(
        date,
        term,
        rate = .mean,
        rate_source = paste(selected_model, "forecast")
      )
  }
}

          p(
            "Rates do not exhibit any true seasonality as the plot reveals no similar movements or values within similar times in the year. This inconsistent pattern suggests that changes that appear to correspond in time may be caused by the similar timing of external political or economic factors, not rates themselves. This is an important insight, but it does not indicate true seasonality."
          )
        ),

        div(
          class = "main-panel-card",
          h3("Term Spread"),
          plotOutput("spread_plot", height = "320px"),
          p(
            "Higher points in the line indicate a greater difference in rates paid on the respective shorter and longer term CDs, such as 6 month versus 12 month and 6 month versus 24 month CDs. As the plot moves closer to zero, represented by the dashed line, the benefit of a longer term decreases. The upward trend on the left side and its change to a downward trend verifies the observations in the core plot, revealing the diminishing benefit of longer term CDs since the peak, along with the convergence of rates in more recent observations."
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ),

  tabPanel(
    "Decompose",
    sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
        selectInput(
          "decomp_term",
          "Select CD term:",
          choices = term_choices,
          selected = "12 Month"
        ),
        radioButtons(
          "decomp_type",
          "Decomposition method:",
          choices = c("STL", "Classical"),
          selected = "STL"
        )
      ),
      mainPanel(
        div(
          class = "main-panel-card",
          plotOutput("decomp_plot", height = "620px"),
          p(
            strong("Interpretation guide:"),
            " STL decomposition performs slightly better than classical decomposition. The series shows a sharp increasing trend that converts into a mild to moderate downward trend. Seasonality is practically non-existent, indicated by the minuscule range in the seasonal component."
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ),

  tabPanel(
    "Forecast",
    sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
        selectInput(
          "forecast_term",
          "Select CD term:",
          choices = term_choices,
          selected = "12 Month"
        ),
        sliderInput(
          "horizon",
          "Forecast horizon, in months:",
          min = 3,
          max = 24,
          value = 12,
          step = 1
        ),
        sliderInput(
          "holdout",
          "Holdout test size, in months:",
          min = 6,
          max = 18,
          value = 12,
          step = 1
        ),
        radioButtons(
          "forecast_model",
          "Model to emphasize:",
          choices = model_choices,
          selected = "Mean"
        )
      ),
      mainPanel(
        div(
          class = "main-panel-card",
          h3("Forecast Plot"),
          plotOutput("forecast_plot", height = "420px")
        ),

        div(
          class = "main-panel-card",
          h3("Accuracy Table on Holdout Set"),
          tableOutput("accuracy_table")
        ),

        div(
          class = "main-panel-card",
          h3("Recommendation"),
          verbatimTextOutput("forecast_recommendation")
        )
      )
    )
  ),

  tabPanel(
    "Simulator",
    sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
        dateInput(
          "invest_date",
          "Date invested:",
          value = as.Date(max_date),
          min = as.Date(min_date),
          max = as.Date(max_future_date)
        ),
        radioButtons(
          "sim_model",
          "Forecast model for future dates:",
          choices = model_choices,
          selected = "Mean"
        ),
        numericInput(
          "initial_amount",
          "Initial amount invested:",
          value = 1000,
          min = 1,
          step = 100
        )
      ),
      mainPanel(
        div(
          class = "main-panel-card",
          h3("Estimated CD Value at Maturity"),
          plotOutput("sim_plot", height = "380px")
        ),

        div(
          class = "main-panel-card",
          h3("Simulation Table"),
          tableOutput("sim_table"),
          p(
            "Due to the illiquidity of CDs, the rate at which a CD is opened cannot change. Calculating its value at maturity is done by using the rate observed at the date it is opened. If the investment date selected is outside the scope of the data, the corresponding rate is determined from the forecasting model selected."
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )
)

# -----------------------------
# 4. Server
# -----------------------------

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  explore_base <- reactive({
    req(input$explore_terms)

    cd |>
      filter(
        term %in% input$explore_terms,
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      )
  })

  output$core_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_sa) seasonally_adjust_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      autoplot(rate) +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_sa,
          "Seasonally Adjusted National Average CD Rates",
          "National Average CD Rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Term"
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$seasonal_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_detrended) detrend_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      gg_season(rate, labels = "both") +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_detrended,
          "Detrended Seasonal Plot",
          "Seasonal Plot"
        ),
        x = "Month",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Year"
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$spread_plot <- renderPlot({
    spread_data <- cd |>
      as_tibble() |>
      filter(
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      ) |>
      select(date, term, rate) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = rate) |>
      mutate(
        `24 minus 6 Month` = `24 Month` - `6 Month`,
        `12 minus 6 Month` = `12 Month` - `6 Month`
      ) |>
      select(date, `24 minus 6 Month`, `12 minus 6 Month`) |>
      pivot_longer(
        -date,
        names_to = "spread",
        values_to = "value"
      ) |>
      filter(!is.na(value))

    ggplot(spread_data, aes(x = date, y = value, color = spread)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
      labs(
        title = "CD Term Spreads",
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate spread, percentage points",
        color = "Spread"
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$decomp_plot <- renderPlot({
    one_series <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$decomp_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date) |>
      as_tsibble(index = date)

    if (input$decomp_type == "STL") {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
        components()
    } else {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(classical_decomposition(rate, type = "additive")) |>
        components()
    }

    autoplot(fit) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          input$decomp_type,
          "decomposition for",
          input$decomp_term,
          "CD rates"
        )
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  forecast_results <- reactive({
    fit_forecast_models(
      cd,
      input$forecast_term,
      input$holdout,
      input$horizon
    )
  })

  output$forecast_plot <- renderPlot({
    res <- forecast_results()

    model_to_show <- input$forecast_model

    fc <- res$future_fc |>
      filter(.model == model_to_show)

    history <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$forecast_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date) |>
      as_tsibble(index = date)

    autoplot(fc, history) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          model_to_show,
          "forecast for",
          input$forecast_term,
          "CD rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)"
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$accuracy_table <- renderTable({
    forecast_results()$accuracy |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(.model, ME, RMSE, MAE) |>
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
  })

  output$forecast_recommendation <- renderText({
    acc <- forecast_results()$accuracy
    best <- acc$.model[1]

    paste0(
      "Recommended model based on current holdout: ", best, "\n\n",
      "Reason: it has the lowest RMSE on the selected holdout period. RMSE is useful here because CD rates are measured in percentage points and larger errors are penalized more heavily. Still, the recommendation can change if the holdout size changes, so the app allows sensitivity checks. A holdout size of 8, 9, 10, and 16 months favors the Naive model, whereas everything else in the 6-18 month range favors ARIMA."
    )
  })

  sim_data <- reactive({
    invest_ym <- yearmonth(input$invest_date)

    sim_rates <- get_simulation_rates(
      data = cd,
      invest_ym = invest_ym,
      selected_model = input$sim_model
    )

    validate(
      need(nrow(sim_rates) > 0, "No rates are available for the selected investment month.")
    )

    sim_rates |>
      mutate(
        term_months = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(term), "\\d+")),
        initial_amount = input$initial_amount,
        maturity_value = initial_amount * (1 + rate / 100 / 12) ^ term_months,
        interest_earned = maturity_value - initial_amount
      )
  })

  output$sim_plot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(sim_data(), aes(x = term, y = maturity_value, fill = term)) +
      geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2))),
        vjust = -0.4
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          "Projected Value at CD Maturity",
          ifelse(
            yearmonth(input$invest_date) > max_date,
            paste("using", input$sim_model, "forecasted rates"),
            "using observed historical rates"
          )
        ),
        x = "CD Term",
        y = "Maturity value"
      ) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$sim_table <- renderTable({
    sim_data() |>
      transmute(
        Term = term,
        `Investment Month` = as.character(date),
        `Rate Source` = rate_source,
        `Rate (%)` = round(rate, 3),
        `Initial Amount` = dollar(initial_amount),
        `Estimated Maturity Value` = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2)),
        `Estimated Interest Earned` = dollar(round(interest_earned, 2))
      )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(fpp3)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)

# -----------------------------
# 1. Data preparation
# -----------------------------

read_fred_cd <- function(series_id, term_months) {
  url <- paste0("https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=", series_id)

  read.csv(url) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      date = yearmonth(observation_date),
      term = term_months,
      rate = .data[[series_id]]
    ) |>
    select(date, term, rate) |>
    filter(
      date >= yearmonth("2021 Apr"),
      date <= yearmonth("2026 Apr"),
      !is.na(rate)
    )
}

cd <- bind_rows(
  read_fred_cd("NDR6MCD", 6),
  read_fred_cd("NDR12MCD", 12),
  read_fred_cd("NDR24MCD", 24)
) |>
  mutate(
    term = factor(
      term,
      levels = c(6, 12, 24),
      labels = c("6 Month", "12 Month", "24 Month")
    )
  ) |>
  as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)

min_date <- min(cd$date)
max_date <- max(cd$date)
max_future_date <- max_date + 24
term_choices <- levels(cd$term)
model_choices <- c("Mean", "ARIMA", "TSLM", "Naive")

# -----------------------------
# 2. Helper functions
# -----------------------------

months_between <- function(start_ym, end_ym) {
  start_date <- as.Date(start_ym)
  end_date <- as.Date(end_ym)

  12 * (year(end_date) - year(start_date)) +
    (month(end_date) - month(start_date))
}

seasonally_adjust_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = season_adjust) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

detrend_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = rate - trend) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

fit_forecast_models <- function(data, selected_term, holdout_size, horizon) {
  one_series <- data |>
    filter(term == selected_term) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    select(date, rate) |>
    arrange(date) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date)

  req(holdout_size < nrow(one_series))

  train_n <- nrow(one_series) - holdout_size

  train <- one_series |>
    slice_head(n = train_n)

  test <- one_series |>
    slice_tail(n = holdout_size)

  fits <- train |>
    model(
      Mean = MEAN(rate),
      Naive = NAIVE(rate),
      ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
      TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
    )

  test_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = holdout_size)

  future_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = horizon)

  acc <- test_fc |>
    accuracy(test) |>
    arrange(RMSE)

  list(
    train = train,
    test = test,
    fits = fits,
    test_fc = test_fc,
    future_fc = future_fc,
    accuracy = acc
  )
}

get_simulation_rates <- function(data, invest_ym, selected_model) {
  if (invest_ym <= max_date) {
    data |>
      filter(date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      mutate(rate_source = "Observed historical rate")
  } else {
    h_needed <- months_between(max_date, invest_ym)

    fits <- data |>
      model(
        Mean = MEAN(rate),
        Naive = NAIVE(rate),
        ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
        TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
      )

    fits |>
      forecast(h = h_needed) |>
      filter(.model == selected_model, date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      transmute(
        date,
        term,
        rate = .mean,
        rate_source = paste(selected_model, "forecast")
      )
  }
}

plot_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

    cd |>
      filter(
        term %in% input$explore_terms,
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      )
  })

  output$core_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_sa) seasonally_adjust_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      autoplot(rate) +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_sa,
          "Seasonally Adjusted National Average CD Rates",
          "National Average CD Rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Term"
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$seasonal_plot <- renderPlot({
    data <- explore_base()
    plot_data <- if (input$use_detrended) detrend_cd(data) else data

    plot_data |>
      gg_season(rate, labels = "both") +
      labs(
        title = ifelse(
          input$use_detrended,
          "Detrended Seasonal Plot",
          "Seasonal Plot"
        ),
        x = "Month",
        y = "Rate (%)",
        color = "Year"
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$spread_plot <- renderPlot({
    spread_data <- cd |>
      as_tibble() |>
      filter(
        date >= yearmonth(input$date_range[1]),
        date <= yearmonth(input$date_range[2])
      ) |>
      select(date, term, rate) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = rate) |>
      mutate(
        `24 minus 6 Month` = `24 Month` - `6 Month`,
        `12 minus 6 Month` = `12 Month` - `6 Month`
      ) |>
      select(date, `24 minus 6 Month`, `12 minus 6 Month`) |>
      pivot_longer(
        -date,
        names_to = "spread",
        values_to = "value"
      ) |>
      filter(!is.na(value))

    ggplot(spread_data, aes(x = date, y = value, color = spread)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
      labs(
        title = "CD Term Spreads",
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate spread, percentage points",
        color = "Spread"
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$decomp_plot <- renderPlot({
    one_series <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$decomp_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date) |>
      as_tsibble(index = date)

    if (input$decomp_type == "STL") {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
        components()
    } else {
      fit <- one_series |>
        model(classical_decomposition(rate, type = "additive")) |>
        components()
    }

    autoplot(fit) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          input$decomp_type,
          "decomposition for",
          input$decomp_term,
          "CD rates"
        )
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  forecast_results <- reactive({
    fit_forecast_models(
      cd,
      input$forecast_term,
      input$holdout,
      input$horizon
    )
  })

  output$forecast_plot <- renderPlot({
    res <- forecast_results()

    model_to_show <- input$forecast_model

    fc <- res$future_fc |>
      filter(.model == model_to_show)

    history <- cd |>
      filter(term == input$forecast_term) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(date, rate) |>
      arrange(date) |>
      as_tsibble(index = date)

    autoplot(fc, history) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          model_to_show,
          "forecast for",
          input$forecast_term,
          "CD rates"
        ),
        x = "Date",
        y = "Rate (%)"
      ) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$accuracy_table <- renderTable({
    forecast_results()$accuracy |>
      as_tibble() |>
      select(.model, ME, RMSE, MAE) |>
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
  })

  output$forecast_recommendation <- renderText({
    acc <- forecast_results()$accuracy
    best <- acc$.model[1]

    paste0(
      "Recommended model based on current holdout: ", best, "\n\n",
      "Reason: it has the lowest RMSE on the selected holdout period. RMSE is useful here because CD rates are measured in percentage points and larger errors are penalized more heavily. Still, the recommendation can change if the holdout size changes, so the app allows sensitivity checks. A holdout size of 8, 9, 10, and 16 months favors the Naive model, whereas everything else in the 6-18 month range favors ARIMA."
    )
  })

  sim_data <- reactive({
    invest_ym <- yearmonth(input$invest_date)

    sim_rates <- get_simulation_rates(
      data = cd,
      invest_ym = invest_ym,
      selected_model = input$sim_model
    )

    validate(
      need(nrow(sim_rates) > 0, "No rates are available for the selected investment month.")
    )

    sim_rates |>
      mutate(
        term_months = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(term), "\\d+")),
        initial_amount = input$initial_amount,
        maturity_value = initial_amount * (1 + rate / 100 / 12) ^ term_months,
        interest_earned = maturity_value - initial_amount
      )
  })

  output$sim_plot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(sim_data(), aes(x = term, y = maturity_value, fill = term)) +
      geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2))),
        vjust = -0.4
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          "Projected Value at CD Maturity",
          ifelse(
            yearmonth(input$invest_date) > max_date,
            paste("using", input$sim_model, "forecasted rates"),
            "using observed historical rates"
          )
        ),
        x = "CD Term",
        y = "Maturity value"
      ) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
      plot_theme
  })

  output$sim_table <- renderTable({
    sim_data() |>
      transmute(
        Term = term,
        `Investment Month` = as.character(date),
        `Rate Source` = rate_source,
        `Rate (%)` = round(rate, 3),
        `Initial Amount` = dollar(initial_amount),
        `Estimated Maturity Value` = dollar(round(maturity_value, 2)),
        `Estimated Interest Earned` = dollar(round(interest_earned, 2))
      )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(fpp3)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)

# -----------------------------
# 1. Data preparation
# -----------------------------

read_fred_cd <- function(series_id, term_months) {
  url <- paste0("https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=", series_id)

  read.csv(url) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      date = yearmonth(observation_date),
      term = term_months,
      rate = .data[[series_id]]
    ) |>
    select(date, term, rate) |>
    filter(
      date >= yearmonth("2021 Apr"),
      date <= yearmonth("2026 Apr"),
      !is.na(rate)
    )
}

cd <- bind_rows(
  read_fred_cd("NDR6MCD", 6),
  read_fred_cd("NDR12MCD", 12),
  read_fred_cd("NDR24MCD", 24)
) |>
  mutate(
    term = factor(
      term,
      levels = c(6, 12, 24),
      labels = c("6 Month", "12 Month", "24 Month")
    )
  ) |>
  as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)

min_date <- min(cd$date)
max_date <- max(cd$date)
max_future_date <- max_date + 24
term_choices <- levels(cd$term)
model_choices <- c("Mean", "ARIMA", "TSLM", "Naive")

# -----------------------------
# 2. Helper functions
# -----------------------------

months_between <- function(start_ym, end_ym) {
  start_date <- as.Date(start_ym)
  end_date <- as.Date(end_ym)

  12 * (year(end_date) - year(start_date)) +
    (month(end_date) - month(start_date))
}

seasonally_adjust_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = season_adjust) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

detrend_cd <- function(data) {
  data |>
    model(stl = STL(rate ~ season(window = "periodic"))) |>
    components() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(date, term, rate = rate - trend) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date, key = term)
}

fit_forecast_models <- function(data, selected_term, holdout_size, horizon) {
  one_series <- data |>
    filter(term == selected_term) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    select(date, rate) |>
    arrange(date) |>
    as_tsibble(index = date)

  req(holdout_size < nrow(one_series))

  train_n <- nrow(one_series) - holdout_size

  train <- one_series |>
    slice_head(n = train_n)

  test <- one_series |>
    slice_tail(n = holdout_size)

  fits <- train |>
    model(
      Mean = MEAN(rate),
      Naive = NAIVE(rate),
      ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
      TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
    )

  test_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = holdout_size)

  future_fc <- fits |>
    forecast(h = horizon)

  acc <- test_fc |>
    accuracy(test) |>
    arrange(RMSE)

  list(
    train = train,
    test = test,
    fits = fits,
    test_fc = test_fc,
    future_fc = future_fc,
    accuracy = acc
  )
}

get_simulation_rates <- function(data, invest_ym, selected_model) {
  if (invest_ym <= max_date) {
    data |>
      filter(date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      mutate(rate_source = "Observed historical rate")
  } else {
    h_needed <- months_between(max_date, invest_ym)

    fits <- data |>
      model(
        Mean = MEAN(rate),
        Naive = NAIVE(rate),
        ARIMA = ARIMA(rate),
        TSLM = TSLM(rate ~ trend() + season())
      )

    fits |>
      forecast(h = h_needed) |>
      filter(.model == selected_model, date == invest_ym) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      transmute(
        date,
        term,
        rate = .mean,
        rate_source = paste(selected_model, "forecast")
      )
  }
}

plot_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "#6b7280"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#e5e7eb"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )
```
